title: Azure DNS and Load Balancing

header.html: Configure Azure DNS; configure an internal or public load balancer; troubleshoot load balancing
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Azure DNS

Azure DNS hosts DNS zones and answers queries from Microsoft's global name servers.

Zone type Use
Public DNS zone Resolves names on the internet (for example contoso.com); delegate the domain by setting the registrar's name servers (NS) to the four Azure name servers
Private DNS zone Resolves names inside virtual networks (for example internal.contoso.com); link the zone to VNets; auto-registration adds VM records automatically
Record type Purpose
A / AAAA Name to IPv4 / IPv6 address
CNAME Name to another name (alias); not allowed at the zone apex
MX Mail servers
TXT Text, verification, SPF
NS / SOA Zone delegation and authority
Alias record Points a record at an Azure resource (public IP, load balancer, Traffic Manager, Front Door); works at the apex and updates automatically

Exam tip

. "The apex domain must point to an Azure public IP or load balancer and follow IP changes" = an alias record. VMs resolve each other by name inside a VNet = private DNS zone (with auto-registration).

2Azure Load Balancer

Azure Load Balancer is a layer 4 (TCP and UDP) load balancer that spreads inbound flows across healthy instances.

Type Use
Public load balancer Internet-facing frontend (public IP)
Internal load balancer Private frontend IP inside a VNet
Component Role
Frontend IP Where clients connect
Backend pool The VMs or scale set instances receiving traffic
Health probe Checks instance health (TCP, HTTP, HTTPS); unhealthy instances get no traffic
Load-balancing rule Maps frontend IP and port to backend pool and port
Inbound NAT rule Forwards one frontend port to one VM (for example RDP to a specific VM)
Outbound rules Control outbound SNAT for backend instances

Distribution uses a 5-tuple hash (source IP and port, destination IP and port, protocol); session persistence (source IP) keeps a client on the same instance.

SKUs: Standard (zone-redundant, secure by default, needs an NSG to allow traffic, SLA) and Basic (being retired [Verify live]).

3Troubleshooting load balancing

Symptom Likely cause
No traffic reaches backends Health probe failing; NSG blocking the AzureLoadBalancer service tag or the client traffic
One VM gets no traffic Probe fails on that VM, or the app is not listening on the probe port
Cannot reach the frontend NSG blocks the port; Standard LB needs an NSG allow rule
Outbound failures SNAT exhaustion: use outbound rules or a NAT gateway
Exam tip

. Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) = Azure Load Balancer. HTTP routing, URL paths and WAF = Application Gateway (layer 7). DNS-based global routing = Traffic Manager. Beyond the study guide

Exam tip

. Layer 4 = Azure Load Balancer; layer 7 = Application Gateway. Match the layer to the requirement.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company wants contoso.com (the zone apex) to point to a load balancer's public IP and follow IP changes. What should be created?

  • AAn alias record
  • BA CNAME at the apex
  • CAn MX record
  • DA TXT record
Show the answer

Answer: A. Alias records work at the apex and track the Azure resource.

S2VMs in a virtual network must resolve each other by name, with records created automatically. What should be used?

  • AA public DNS zone with a record for every virtual machine
  • BA private DNS zone linked to the VNet with auto-registration
  • CA hosts file on each VM that is updated by an administrator
  • DAn MX record for every virtual machine in the virtual network
Show the answer

Answer: B. Private zones with auto-registration add VM records.

S3A load balancer's backend VMs receive no traffic. The health probe fails. Which NSG issue is common?

  • AThe NSG allows all traffic from the internet to the backend
  • BA missing tag on the load balancer frontend IP address
  • CA resource lock on the backend pool that blocks health checks
  • DThe NSG blocks the AzureLoadBalancer service tag
Show the answer

Answer: D. Probes come from the AzureLoadBalancer tag and must be allowed.

S4Which load balancer type has a private frontend IP address?

  • APublic
  • BGlobal
  • CBasic only
  • DInternal
Show the answer

Answer: D. Internal load balancers use a private frontend IP.

S5Which rule forwards one frontend port to a single VM for RDP?

  • ALoad-balancing rule
  • BInbound NAT rule
  • COutbound rule
  • DHealth probe
Show the answer

Answer: B. Inbound NAT rules map a frontend port to one backend VM.

S6What OSI layer does Azure Load Balancer work at?

  • ALayer 4
  • BLayer 7
  • CLayer 2
  • DLayer 1
Show the answer

Answer: A. It balances TCP and UDP flows at layer 4.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What record type points a name to another name?

Show the answer

CNAME.

R2What must you change at your registrar to delegate a domain to Azure DNS?

Show the answer

The name servers (NS records).

R3What does a health probe do?

Show the answer

Checks backend health so unhealthy instances get no traffic.

R4What does Standard Load Balancer require for inbound traffic?

Show the answer

An NSG rule that allows it.

R5What does a private DNS zone link do?

Show the answer

Lets VNets resolve names in the zone.

R6Which service is the layer 7 option?

Show the answer

Application Gateway.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Azure DNS public zones (delegate NS), private zones (linked, auto-registration), alias records at the apex
Load Balancer layer 4; public or internal; frontend, pool, probe, rules, NAT rules
Troubleshoot probes, NSG on AzureLoadBalancer, SNAT exhaustion
Others Application Gateway (layer 7), Traffic Manager (DNS-based)
